title: dedicated-autoscaler: better burst controls, throughput guarantees and utilization reporting
author: Priya Raman
description: Motivation: Dedicated fleets occasionally exhaust burst tokens under transient load spikes which causes degraded throughput and unexpected backpressure. This PR improves the autoscaler burst controls and reporting so SREs and customers can understand and tune throughput guarantees. Goals: 1) Add an adaptive burst token smoothing algorithm that prevents immediate token exhaustion on short spikes while preserving long-term throughput guarantees. 2) Surface per-fleet and per-route burst utilization metrics and a derived 'burst headroom' signal used by the autoscaler decision path. 3) Expose new config knobs for throughput guarantees (min_throughput_pct) and a configurable burst window for backfills. 4) Add end-to-end tests and docs for operators. Changes include runtime logic, autoscaler controller changes, metric names and dashboards, and CLI/console config plumbing. Checklist: - [x] Kernel-safe burst token adjustment in serving runtime - [x] Autoscaler uses burst headroom signal in decision path - [x] Per-fleet and per-route utilization reporting to observability pipeline - [x] New config flags validated and documented - [x] Unit + integration tests - [x] Manual canary on staging for 48h Summary of impact: expected to reduce burst exhaustion incidents by smoothing short spikes while retaining configured throughput guarantees. No behavioral change for customers who keep existing defaults. Note: this touches autoscaler and serving runtime; rollout plan: incremental canary on dedicated fleets, opt-in config exposure, monitoring and auto-rollback on SLO regressions.
